newsitem.title: USA: Caliber System to cut 1,500 Viking Freight jobs.
newsitem.headline: Caliber System to cut 1,500 Viking Freight jobs.

text.p: Calibre System Inc. said Thursday it will close 30 terminals and cut about 1,500 jobs at Viking Freight Inc. in 1997 in an ongoing restructuring of the money-losing subsidiary.
Calibre also said Rodger G. Marticke, 48, will become president and chief executive of Viking when Ronald G. Pelzel, 56, retires from those positions at year's end.

Calibre, formerly Roadway Services, Inc., said San Jose, Calif.-based Viking will report an operating loss for the fourth quarter. The loss will be similar to that in the third quarter and depress Calibre's profits, the company said.
Calibre, based in Akron, Ohio, did not provide details but said it expects to be profitable for the quarter and full year.
It also said it will freeze the wages of all Viking salaried employees for the first half of 1997, "or until operating results improve."
"We are considering all options for Viking," said Daniel J. Sullivan, chairman, president and CEO of Calibre System.

"Studies are being conducted, under my direction, by internal personnel and outside consulting teams, which include industry experts as well as corporate re-engineering, consolidation and cost reduction specialists."

Marticke has been president of Calibre Logistics, a contract logistics provider based in Hudson, Ohio, since Oct. 1, 1995. He held several senior management positions with Calibre from 1993 through 1995.
Thomas I. Escott, 44, will replace Marticke as president of Calibre Logistics. Escott has served as the subsidiary's vice president of sales and marketing since Jan. 1, 1994.
Calibre changed its name in January when it spun off its Roadway Express Inc. trucking company.
Its stock was unchanged at $19.75 on the New York Stock Exchange at midday.
